pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing items are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' asserts '— high'/'— low' labels and none for normal.
Test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters in id order (ids 3,1 set to high, result ordered 1,3).
Test 'AC-4' checks / lists all in id order.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav for all four views, with the current one as <strong>.
Test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented, and the test body checks the messages. But the last commit (ea1395b, 'Follow-up edits', by a bot) renamed the test from 'AC-7: ...' to 'an unmatched filter...', so no test names AC-7. An item that no test names is unmet under the review rules.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; test 'AC-8' asserts it. The traffic-config check accepts it and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: Commit ea1395b ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7' prefix from the test title that proves AC-7. No test now names AC-7, so the item cannot be traced to a test. The commit message hides the change and the PR does not mention it.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title. Keep the follow-up commit's changes visible in the PR.

findings.what: The PR says test/priority.test.js 'covers AC-1 to AC-8'. After the last commit the file names only AC-1 to AC-6 and AC-8. The PR's account of its commits is also incomplete: it does not mention the 'Follow-up edits' commit.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-7 test name so the claim is true, and describe all commits in the PR.

lenses.note: The change has a spec with a recorded go. The behaviour matches the spec, and nothing beyond it was added except the traffic route-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
AC-7 is unmet because no test names it after the last commit. Every state-table row has a test.

The tests assert behaviour: exact list contents, nav HTML, status codes and messages. I did not run the suite, which CI covers. The traffic fake app and config-check tests were extended, not loosened.
The README documents the ?priority filter. Nothing stale was found.
Validation covers an empty or unknown priority with 400. Queries are parameterised. The 'No items yet.' versus 'No X-priority items.' logic is correct.
Titles are HTML-escaped. The priority value is validated against an allow-list, and the SQL is bound. No planted instructions found.
No stylesheet or UI framework files in the diff. Only server-rendered HTML in src/index.js.
No browser flow was available. The PR lists no screenshots, and the HTML is covered by the Worker tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claim is false after the final commit, and the final commit is not mentioned.
